 UAE Confirms Two-Day Paid National Day Holiday
 3 hours ago 2 min read Private-sector employees across the UAE will receive paid leave on 2 and 3 December 2026, with an option to extend the National Day break through annual leave. 
 Image Courtesy: Sanctum Consulting The UAE Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MoHRE) has confirmed a two-day paid public holiday for private-sector employees to mark the country's 55th Eid Al Etihad, also known as National Day. 
 The holiday will fall on Wednesday, 2 December, and Thursday, 3 December 2026, allowing employees across private-sector establishments to participate in the national celebrations. 
 The announcement follows the UAE's established public holiday framework and provides employers and employees with confirmed dates for planning workplace schedules and annual leave. 
 How Employees Can Extend the Holiday 
 Friday, 4 December, remains a regular working day for private-sector employees whose schedules include Fridays. 
 However, employees who normally have Saturday and Sunday off can request one day of annual leave on Friday, creating a five-day break from Wednesday, 2 December, through Sunday, 6 December. 
 The arrangement would allow eligible employees to return to work on Monday, 7 December, subject to their employer's approval of the additional leave. 
 Federal Government Employees Receive Three Days 
 The Federal Authority for Government Human Resources has separately confirmed a three-day holiday for federal government employees, running from Wednesday, 2 December, to Friday, 4 December. 
 With the weekend included, many federal employees will enjoy five consecutive days off before official working hours resume on Monday, 7 December. 
 The different holiday arrangements reflect the working schedules and official announcements applicable to the public and private sectors. 
 Supporting Employee Leave Planning 
 Eid Al Etihad commemorates the establishment of the UAE on 2 December 1971 and is one of the country's principal national celebrations. 
 For employers, the confirmed holiday dates provide an opportunity to organise staffing arrangements and communicate leave entitlements ahead of December. 
 Employees planning additional time off are encouraged to review their annual leave balances and obtain approval before making travel arrangements. 
 The announcement also reinforces the importance of clear workplace communication around public holidays, allowing employees to plan their personal commitments while businesses maintain operational continuity. 
 Sources: UAE Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MoHRE); Federal Authority for Government Human Resources (FAHR); UAE Government; The National; Gulf News; Arabian Business
